title: Post-incident hardening: eviction spike, reservation sizing, and burst-policy refinements for Dedicated clusters
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: On 2026-02-24 a Dedicated cluster in us-west-2 experienced an eviction spike that caused request latency regressions and a short (35m) throughput outage for several customers on reserved pools. Contributing factors were (1) reservation mis-sizing for a new customer cohort, (2) a burst policy that allowed transient overcommit which exhausted burst credits and then aggressively evicted low-priority tenants, and (3) a noisy-tenant training job that briefly consumed >3x expected GPU memory and I/O. This ticket tracks the post-incident follow-ups to harden capacity isolation and reservation sizing and to refine burst behavior so we avoid correlated evictions in the future.
incident_timeline: 2026-02-24 02:12 UTC: Autoscaler noted GPU utilization rising above 92% in reserved pool rsv-usw2-14.
2026-02-24 02:18 UTC: Burst credits on the pool exhausted; autoscaler delayed additional allocations due to conservative cool-down setting.
2026-02-24 02:20 UTC: Kernel eviction controller started preempting lower-QoS workloads to free memory; several customer routes reported increased 95th pct latency.
2026-02-24 02:40 UTC: Ops triggered emergency capacity add (manual scale-up) and applied temp QoS pin for business-critical tenants.
2026-02-24 02:57 UTC: Noisy tenant identified (internal experimental training job) and throttled; cluster stabilized by 03:00 UTC.
2026-02-24 03:10 UTC: Post-incident mitigation: rollback of recent reservation sizing change for cohort B and created temporary segregation rules.
root_causes: Reservation plan for cohort B used historical utilization percentiles but failed to account for peak synthetic workloads introduced by a new customer integration, resulting in a 25-40% under-allocation margin.
Burst policy semantics allowed short windows of >100% capacity (credit burn) without a progressive backoff, causing simultaneous credit exhaustion across many pools and triggering eviction cascade.
Noisy tenant submitted a long-running job with unintended I/O patterns; lack of tenant-level IO cgroup throttling allowed it to compete aggressively with inference latency-sensitive tasks.
Monitoring alerts were present but thresholds were set to aggregated signals; individual reservation-level degradation alerts were not firing fast enough.
blast_radius_and_impact: Affected: 4 reserved pools, 3 paying customers experienced degraded SLOs (elevated p95 latency).
Duration: ~35 minutes of unstable latency, ~12 minutes of active request failures for one customer route before failover policies engaged.
Financial: Estimated partial SLA credits for two customers; cost to ops for emergency scale-up (~$3.2k equivalent).
Reputation: One customer support escalation; incident postmortem requested by Customer Success.
short_term_mitigations_done: Rolled back recent reservation shrink for cohort B (2026-02-24 03:00 UTC).
Applied manual QoS pin to preserve capacity for high-SLO customers during remediation window.
Throttled the noisy internal training job and added an immediate runtime guard to prevent identical job submission patterns.
Lowered autoscaler cool-down for the affected dedicated pools from 10m to 2m as temporary measure.
action_items: AI-1: Implement reservation-sizing discovery utility that ingests request-level p95/p99 and peak-concurrency traces and recommends reservation margins. Owner: Lina Chen. Due: 2026-03-21.
AI-2: Redesign burst policy to include progressive backoff and randomized credit replenishment to avoid synchronized exhaustion. Owner: Diego Morales. Due: 2026-03-28.
AI-3: Add tenant-level IO and GPU-memory cgroup controls and enforce a default QoS floor for inference routes. Owner: Rafael Ortega. Due: 2026-04-09.

AI-4: Create reservation-level alerting (per-pool p95 tokens, memory pressure) with runbook links and automated mitigation steps (scale hint + temporary pin). Owner: Ops SRE team (owner: Mei Wong). Due: 2026-03-14.
AI-5: Run chaos-capacity test that simulates noisy tenant memory and I/O spikes across 10% of dedicated pools before each release. Owner: Reliability Eng (owner: Omar Khan). Due: 2026-04-16.
AI-6: Produce customer-impact communication template and coordinate SLA credit calculation with Finance and CS. Owner: Sarah Blake (CS). Due: 2026-03-10.
AI-7: Add a post-deploy verification checklist for reservation changes that includes synthetic load validation at 2x expected peak. Owner: Product (owner: Priya Nair). Due: 2026-03-18.
AI-8: Postmortem doc and runbook consolidation: consolidate this ticket's learnings into the Dedicated Incident Runbook. Owner: Asha Patel. Due: 2026-03-07.
acceptance_criteria: Reservation-sizing utility is merged to main and has an automated job that outputs weekly recommendations for each reserved pool.
Burst policy change rolled out to canary pools without causing increased cold-start latency and observed to reduce correlated credit exhaustion in synthetic tests.
Tenant-level cgroup controls enabled in one pilot region and show no regressions in latency for pinned routes.
New alerts fire at pool-level and trigger documented automated mitigations; on-call runbook verified in tabletop exercise.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement and unit-test code changes in feature branch.
2) Run synthetic stress tests in staging and a designated canary region (use canary pools flagged in tag 'canary-dedicated').
3) Gradual rollout to 10% dedicated pools, monitor 1h/6h/24h windows for p95, eviction counts and credit utilization.
4) If metrics stable, expand to 50% then to full fleet during low-traffic weekend window with Ops support.

2026-03-10: Customer communications prepared; Finance confirmed SLA credit calc method; awaiting CS approval. (Sarah Blake)

review_feedback_and_notes: Design feedback (Product): Ensure reservation tool outputs both absolute GPU vRAM and token-throughput targets so PMs can trade cost vs SLO.
Security review: cgroup enforcement requires review for multi-tenant kernel flags; security will do a focused review before region-wide rollout. (Findings due 2026-03-20)
Legal: No new compliance impact expected but document customer-facing wording for SLA credits.
Ops note: Consider adding a fast-path 'emergency pin' API to avoid manual console steps during incidents.

Lina to add a dashboard and weekly email for reservation recommendations (due 2026-03-21).
Rafael to run the first pilot of cgroup limits in us-west-2 with two non-critical customers (due 2026-04-09).

notes_for_release_notes: Resolved immediate causes; long-term fixes include reservation-sizing utility, burst policy progressive backoff, tenant-level cgroup enforcement and new per-reservation alerts. Will include a short blurb and customer guidance in runtime-1.21 release notes.
